successors.name: Roman Republic
successors.text: the Ligurian country after the colonies of Luna and Lucca

ledger.x: The Ligures, a people of north-western Italy with a culturally distinct Bronze Age area of Piedmont, Liguria, western Lombardy and western Emilia.

c. 177 BC: Rome plants Luna and Lucca. 'c. 177 BC: Colonies of Luna and Lucca secured the southern frontier.' The page names the colonies, not their land; the discs are the researcher's reading, and the Apuani page says nothing of confiscation.
155 BC: the Ligurian country passes to Rome.
155 BC: the Italian Ligures cease to resist as a people; Augustus later gave the name an administrative sense as regio IX.

wars.name: Roman conquest of the Ligures
wars.outcome: Roman victory after a long series of campaigns: 238-233 (Gracchus, Lentulus, Fabius), 201 peace with the Ingauni, 187 offensive and 185-181 Ingauni campaigns, the deportation of the Apuani to Samnium in 180, the Statielli enslaved in 173, and Marcellus's last…

certainty.note: Tribal lands with no treaty line; the page gives rivers and mountains (Arno, Magra, Serchio, Var) and the Etruscans as the eastern boundary.
